arbol_de_trazas.nota: El árbol lo arman el `EjecutorDeEtapas` (corrida y etapa) y el decorador de puertos (una traza por llamada a puerto). **Ninguna etapa emite su propio span** — la observabilidad lo prohíbe y señala al ejecutor como el lugar correcto para el desglose. `campos_censurados > 0` es el registro de decisiones actuando: en una consulta ad-hoc no viaja ni el pedido ni la imagen.

politica.por_que: Las 30 consultas de evaluación se trazan **completas** (`el registro de decisiones la política de trazado`). No son dato de un tercero: son obras de nuestro propio held-out, versionadas con el ground truth porque son el **instrumento de medición** (el registro de decisiones). Trazarlas enteras cumple las técnicas avanzadas aisladas por medición, la tabla de tokens, costo y la figura y el criterio de costo sin tocar el compromiso de privacidad.

degradaciones.politica: se cae la fuente `"texto"` y el resto corre con una sola: el `Fusionador` pasa a través con la **visual** (degradación). `fuentes_de_ranking["texto"]` queda ausente **+ degradación** — sin la entrada, la forma declarada del artefacto rechaza la corrida, que es su primera dirección. Es la omisión de etapas en runtime literal: *si falla la rama de texto, el visual*.

entrada.nota_de_retencion: el registro de decisiones (cierra la pregunta por el ciclo de vida de la corrida purgada): **no se persiste nada de un tercero**. Los bytes de la imagen no se guardan nunca —no hay clave que los active— y el `pedido` solo si `[retencion] pedido = true`. Lo que se vacía son **campos**, y que estaban vaciados queda registrado (la regla de qué se versiona): la corrida conserva su `corrida_id`, su ordinal, sus rankings y sus degradaciones, porque borrarla reasignaría el ordinal y un informe que cita la corrida #1 apuntaría a otra ejecución.

aic:12891.texto:
This painting depicts a historical event from the year 390 when Ambrose, the archbishop of Milan, refused to give communion to Emperor Theodosius I until he made public penance for the massacre of thousands of innocents after an insurrection. Theodosius, the last emperor to command the entire Roman Empire, eventually submitted to the archbishop’s moral authority.
The brushwork and arrangement of figures in this composition showcase Alessandro Magnasco’s fluid, energetic style. However, for the elaborate background edifice, an imaginary interpretation of the atrium of an early Christian church, he most likely employed an unidentified specialist in architectural painting.
aic:12891.title: Theodosius Repulsed from the Church by Saint Ambrose

cma:111691.texto: The Jewish synagogue was among Magnasco's most frequently painted subjects, here presented in a mystical and imaginative way. Expansive architectural space creates room for a multitude of tiny, fantastical figures with elongated limbs. These characters respond to the service with emotion and expressive gestures. Flashes of light dash across the surface against a dark, muted palette of earthy tones suggesting an otherworldly presence. The composition invites the viewer to enter the space and experience the service. Though he used characteristic elements of Baroque composition and was strongly influenced by Venetian painting, Magnasco's loose brushwork, elongated figures, and mysterious subject matter set him apart. Magnasco peers into a world of which he was not part: he was not Jewish and probably perceived Jews as outsiders. At the dawn of the Enlightenment in Europe progressive aristocratic families commissioned paintings by Magnasco, suggesting the painter's support for Enlightenment ideals which included religious tolerance, but Magnasco's personal views on Judaism in Italy remain unknown.
cma:111691.title: Interior of a Synagogue

cma:132647.texto: According to Roman Catholic theology, the Assumption is the movement of the Virgin Mary's body and soul into heaven. Thus the central figure of the Virgin dominates this scene of the Assumption, outstretching her arms and supported by two angels as she ascends into heaven. Below, saints surround the Virgin's tomb. St. Peter reaches for the foot of the ascending Virgin, suggesting a connection between heaven and earth. Giovanni Battista Piazzetta created this work as a sketch for his larger altarpiece commissioned in 1743 for the Church of St. James in Zbraslav, near Prague. The Assumption of the Virgin is a rare oil sketch by Piazzetta, and the larger composition adheres closely to this model. One difference between the sketch and the altarpiece is that the saints are illuminated more in the preliminary work. A divine light shines on the faces of the Virgin and the figures below her. Above the other figures, the Virgin appears remote and focuses on heaven as she looks upwards and beyond the painting's borders. The grouping of the figures in the center of this painting creates a vast surrounding space which fittingly gives this altarpiece sketch a sense of monumentality.
cma:132647.title: Sketch for "The Assumption of the Virgin" (for St. James, Zbraslav, near Prague)?

cma:147938.texto: Created as a temple under the Roman emperor Hadrian around the year AD 125, the Pantheon became a Christian church in 609. Significant restoration took place in the early 1700s, a period of renewed attention to early Christian monuments. The site was a major monument of antiquity, an active church, and its portico, visible through the door, held the most important art fair in the city. Panini shows the complexity of this public space by representing foreign tourists, local churchgoers, Roman nobles, and artists mingling under the dome.
cma:147938.title: Interior of the Pantheon, Rome

cma:147938.texto: Panini's depictions of contemporary and ancient Rome were popular with foreigners who visited the city on their Grand Tours.

       https://clevelandart.org/art/1949.187.1 · CC0 1.0

3. **Theodosius Repulsed from the Church by Saint Ambrose**
   Alessandro Magnasco · c. 1705 · Oil on canvas · 18th Century
   Ficha oficial: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/12891

   La obra es una pintura italiana del siglo XVIII que representa un interior arquitectónico imaginado de una iglesia cristiana primitiva, con un estilo fluido y enérgico. [1]
   El interior representado es complejo y muestra una escena histórica con figuras dinámicas, pero no se especifica ni se observa una paleta de tonos fríos ni una atmósfera imponente.
   No hay información suficiente para afirmar que la obra tenga tonos fríos o una presencia imponente.

   **Fuentes**
   [1] “This painting depicts a historical event from the year 390 when Ambrose, the archbishop of Milan, refused to give communion to Emperor Theodosius I until he made public penance for the massacre of thousands of innocents after an insurrection. Theodosius, the last emperor to command the entire Roman Empire, eventually submitted to the archbishop’s moral authority.
The brushwork and arrangement of figures in this composition showcase Alessandro Magnasco’s fluid, energetic style. However, for the elaborate background edifice, an imaginary interpretation of the atrium of an early Christian church, he most likely employed an unidentified specialist in architectural painting.”
       https://www.artic.edu/artworks/12891 · CC BY 4.0
       “Theodosius Repulsed from the Church by Saint Ambrose”, Alessandro Magnasco. Art Institute of Chicago. Texto bajo CC BY 4.0 — https://www.artic.edu/artworks/12891

4. **Interior of the Pantheon, Rome**
   Giovanni Paolo Panini · 1747 · oil on canvas
   Ficha oficial: https://clevelandart.org/art/1974.39

   La pintura representa el interior del Panteón de Roma, un monumento antiguo y restaurado en el siglo XVIII, con una escena que incluye turistas, nobles y artistas bajo la cúpula. [1]
   El espacio interior es amplio y monumental, con una atmósfera solemne y majestuosa, propia de un monumento histórico y religioso importante.
   No se menciona ni se observa que la paleta de colores sea fría, por lo que no se puede asegurar que cumpla con el pedido.

   **Fuentes**
   [1] “Created as a temple under the Roman emperor Hadrian around the year AD 125, the Pantheon became a Christian church in 609. Significant restoration took place in the early 1700s, a period of renewed attention to early Christian monuments. The site was a major monument of antiquity, an active church, and its portico, visible through the door, held the most important art fair in the city. Panini shows the complexity of this public space by representing foreign tourists, local churchgoers, Roman nobles, and artists mingling under the dome.”
       https://clevelandart.org/art/1974.39 · CC0 1.0

5. **Sketch for "The Assumption of the Virgin" (for St. James, Zbraslav, near Prague)?**
   Giovanni Battista Piazzetta · c. 1744 · oil on canvas
   Ficha oficial: https://clevelandart.org/art/1955.165

   La obra es un boceto para un retablo italiano del barroco que representa la Asunción de la Virgen, con una figura central dominante y un sentido de monumentalidad. [1]
   El boceto muestra una iluminación divina que resalta las figuras, pero la descripción indica que los santos están más iluminados y no se menciona una paleta fría ni un interior imponente en tonos fríos.
   No hay evidencia de que la obra utilice tonos fríos ni que represente un interior imponente en ese sentido.

   **Fuentes**
   [1] “According to Roman Catholic theology, the Assumption is the movement of the Virgin Mary's body and soul into heaven. Thus the central figure of the Virgin dominates this scene of the Assumption, outstretching her arms and supported by two angels as she ascends into heaven. Below, saints surround the Virgin's tomb. St. Peter reaches for the foot of the ascending Virgin, suggesting a connection between heaven and earth. Giovanni Battista Piazzetta created this work as a sketch for his larger altarpiece commissioned in 1743 for the Church of St. James in Zbraslav, near Prague. The Assumption of the Virgin is a rare oil sketch by Piazzetta, and the larger composition adheres closely to this model. One difference between the sketch and the altarpiece is that the saints are illuminated more in the preliminary work. A divine light shines on the faces of the Virgin and the figures below her. Above the other figures, the Virgin appears remote and focuses on heaven as she looks upwards and beyond the painting's borders. The grouping of the figures in the center of this painting creates a vast surrounding space which fittingly gives this altarpiece sketch a sense of monumentality.”
       https://clevelandart.org/art/1955.165 · CC0 1.0

nota_de_a8_vs_bd4: 🔴 **Las dos lecturas del libro mayor, y son proyecciones del mismo dato**: la tabla de costo pide el gasto *por etapa* y la atribución de cada llamada lo cuenta *por rol, no por el nombre de la etapa*. nota_de_identidad: Clase 2 (la tabla de identidades): *registro de una ejecución*. La identidad fija **las entradas, no la salida** —una salida no determinista con la misma entrada es el dato que el muestreo fijado, registrado y con su variabilidad medida mide—, así que lleva **ordinal** y la regla de que un id determina su contenido no aplica. El ordinal se **reserva** creando el directorio de forma exclusiva: `1 + n` es un *leer, después escribir* y el barrido es paralelo.
nota_de_la_tabla: degradación/la regla de qué corridas agregan a la tabla: una corrida con degradación **no planificada** no agrega a la tabla C0–C4 —*una C4 que degradó en silencio entraría etiquetada como C4 comportándose como C3*— y una con degradación **planificada** tampoco: es el criterio de respuesta garantizada y se reporta aparte. Una etapa **ausente por configuración** no degrada: no corre, y por eso C0–C3 sí agregan.

El `config_id` hashea la configuración resuelta **menos** las claves de arriba —layout, parámetros de máquina, ruteo, transporte y el precio declarado—, que son **procedencia**: viajan enteras en `configuracion_resuelta` y no mueven la identidad. Un candidato **sin puntaje** degrada igual: ordenar mezclando «puntuado» con «no pude puntuarlo» sería publicar dos escalas en una columna , y los puntajes que sí se pagaron quedan en el artefacto.
